name: Milucra

attributes.attribute: an Irish goddess and sister of Áine
enchanted a lake on Slieve Gullion to gray the hair of swimmers
aged the hero Fionn and was captured by the Fianna

sources: Joyce, Patrick Weston. Ancient Celtic Romances. London: Parkgate Books, 1997, 315+.

text: Milucra, also called Miluchrach, was an Irish goddess and the sister of the better-known goddess Áine. Milucra grew infatuated with the great hero Fionn mac Cumhaill, as did her sister. Áine had sworn she would never sleep with a gray-haired man. Milucra enchanted a lake on Slieve Gullion in Ulster so that it dyed gray the hair of any swimmer. When the young Fionn met a beautiful maiden by the lake, she said her golden ring had fallen into the water. Fionn swam out to fetch it. He found the ring, but when he climbed out his hair had turned gray and his body aged and withered. He was no longer pleasing to the sensuous Áine. The Fianna captured Milucra and forced her to give their leader a drink that restored his youth. His hair stayed silver.
objective: Document Milucra and the enchanted lake that aged Fionn.
